stops.name: Pelly Crossing fuel
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 531235626 (amenity=fuel, Klondike Highway km 463, Pelly Crossing), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Diesel and truck access are assumed, not read: it is one of two fuel stops between Carmacks and Dawson City. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: 60 Petro Express Stewart Crossing
stops.source: Position and name read from OSM way 531235105 (amenity=fuel, brand Shell, 60 Petro Express, 213 Klondike Highway, Stewart Crossing), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Diesel and truck access are assumed, not read: it is the fuel stop at the Silver Trail junction. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Stewart Crossing rest area
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 305366514 (highway=rest_area, unnamed), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Truck parking and an overnight stay are assumed, not read: it is the North Klondike Highway rest area nearest the middle of the 219 miles from Carmacks to Dawson City; the name is descriptive. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Yukon Cardlock Klondike River
stops.source: Position and name read from OSM way 1125224716 (amenity=fuel, Yukon Cardlock), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16, on the North Klondike Highway by the AFD Petroleum depot near the Dempster Highway corner. Truck service read from its name; diesel assumed. A cardlock sells to account holders only. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

corridor.source: New leg for the northern corridor, west (Career 2.0, 2026-11-22): laid out between the two city pins, then routed by Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de) along Klondike Highway.

landmarks.name: Five Finger Rapids (Carmacks to Dawson City)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: Five Finger Rapids, ahead. Four pillars of rock split the Yukon River into five channels, and the sternwheelers bound for Dawson could use only one. Lane discipline is older than the highway.

landmarks.name: Tintina Trench (Carmacks to Dawson City)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: The Tintina Trench, ahead. A fault valley that runs across the Yukon, and a flyway for sandhill cranes every May and September. They make the trip without a logbook.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

bridges.name: Yukon River Bridge
bridges.source: Name read from the curated sheet (Yukon Highways and Public Works, Yukon River bridge at Carmacks (North Klondike Highway); the way carries no bridge name in OpenStreetMap); span derived by projecting its ways (way/264403924) onto the leg's archived road, rescaled to leg miles (curated, 730 ft); what it spans read from the curated sheet. OpenStreetMap, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/.

stops.name: Takhini Gas
stops.source: Position read from OSM node 13849499502 (amenity=fuel, Takhini Gas, Klondike Highway, fuel:diesel=yes, large_vehicles=yes), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Diesel and large-vehicle access read. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Cousins rest area
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 305369410 (highway=rest_area, Cousins Rest Area, operator Government of Yukon, opening_hours=24/7, toilets=yes), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Truck parking and an overnight stay are assumed, not read: the Yukon's rest-area list needs a developer key, so OpenStreetMap's Government of Yukon tags are the only reading; hours read, truck room not. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

landmarks.name: Takhini River
landmarks.source: derived: name and category read from the OpenStreetMap tags of way 1292173286 (Takhini River); placed at the crossing of the road with it on the leg's archived route geometry, rescaled to leg miles. OpenStreetMap, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

billboard_bans.name: Fox Lake Territorial Park
billboard_bans.source: derived 2026-11-22: OpenStreetMap protected-area polygon (Fox Lake Territorial Park) boundary from the planet extract of 2026-11-16 (corridor-5-west-places.md); the stretch of the leg's archived route inside the park or protected area or within 150 m of its boundary, gaps under 2 miles merged (the right of way is carved out of the park, so the road has no private land beside it to stand a board on); widened to the one-mile minimum

stops.name: Yukon Cardlock Klondike River
stops.source: Position and name read from OSM way 1125224716 (amenity=fuel, Yukon Cardlock), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16, on the North Klondike Highway by the AFD Petroleum depot near the Dempster Highway corner. Truck service read from its name; diesel assumed. A cardlock sells to account holders only. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Stewart Crossing rest area
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 305366514 (highway=rest_area, unnamed), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Truck parking and an overnight stay are assumed, not read: it is the North Klondike Highway rest area nearest the middle of the 219 miles from Carmacks to Dawson City; the name is descriptive. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: 60 Petro Express Stewart Crossing
stops.source: Position and name read from OSM way 531235105 (amenity=fuel, brand Shell, 60 Petro Express, 213 Klondike Highway, Stewart Crossing), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Diesel and truck access are assumed, not read: it is the fuel stop at the Silver Trail junction. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Pelly Crossing fuel
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 531235626 (amenity=fuel, Klondike Highway km 463, Pelly Crossing), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Diesel and truck access are assumed, not read: it is one of two fuel stops between Carmacks and Dawson City. Open year round is assumed, not read. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

stops.name: Delta Western, Haines
stops.source: Position and diesel read from OSM node 2058194642 (fuel:diesel=yes), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Tractor-trailer access is assumed, because no source found says either way: freight on these roads moves by tractor-trailer, and a town's diesel on the through highway is where those trucks fuel. hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

stops.name: Trails North, Whitehorse
stops.source: Position and diesel read from OSM way 469609783 (fuel:diesel=yes), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Open year round is assumed for a staffed station in a town on a through highway; not verified. Tractor-trailer access is assumed, because no source found says either way: freight on these roads moves by tractor-trailer, and a town's diesel on the through highway is where those trucks fuel. Parking capacity is not claimed. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.
